cards.title: The Barnacle Button Keeper
cards.characterSkill: Builds a character from a small job, a pretend object, and one gentle worry.
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led paper card when a young writer needs a clear fictional character before starting a tidepool lab scene: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: Place this printable card beside the printed pretend coat pocket and remind the writer that every pocket item is made up on paper: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a short scene where your tidepool lab character notices a tiny change and decides what to do next: ____________________.
cards.characterNamePrompt: Give the fictional tidepool helper a made-up name: ____________________.
cards.pocketItemPrompt: Choose one pretend paper-pocket item, like a shell button, kelp ribbon, or bubble note: ____________________.
cards.wantPrompt: Write what this character wants to fix, learn, or protect in the tidepool lab: ____________________.
cards.worryPrompt: Write one gentle worry that makes the job harder: ____________________.
cards.actionPrompt: Write one careful action the character takes with the pretend pocket item: ____________________.
cards.voicePrompt: Write one line the character says in a curious, careful voice: ____________________.
cards.reviseCharacterPrompt: Revise by adding one habit the character repeats when thinking: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the name, pocket item, and first action: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home slip: Finish this sentence for another tidepool character: In my pretend paper pocket, I keep ____________________.

cards.title: The Ferry Pilot With a Patchwork Oar Tag
cards.characterSkill: Shows character change by giving the character a first idea, a revised idea, and a better choice.
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led paper card to help writers create a fictional ferry character who changes their plan during revision: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: Slide the card under the printed pretend coat pocket flap and frame the pocket item as a paper story prop only: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a scene where the ferry character crosses Revision River and changes one idea before reaching the dock: ____________________.
cards.characterNamePrompt: Name the fictional ferry character with a name that sounds ready for revision: ____________________.
cards.pocketItemPrompt: Write the pretend paper-pocket item that helps them rethink a plan: ____________________.
cards.wantPrompt: Write the first thing the character wants before the ferry ride begins: ____________________.
cards.worryPrompt: Write the worry that makes the character hold too tightly to the first plan: ____________________.
cards.actionPrompt: Write the action that shows the character trying a revised choice: ____________________.
cards.voicePrompt: Write one line in the character's voice before or after the revision: ____________________.
cards.reviseCharacterPrompt: Revise by changing the character's want so it becomes more specific: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write the first plan and the revised plan in two short phrases: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home slip: Invent another Revision River passenger and the paper-pocket clue they carry: ____________________.

cards.title: The Label-Swap Curator
cards.characterSkill: Creates a clue-friendly character with a role, a secret preference, and a non-scary mistake to solve.
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led paper card when a writer needs a fictional museum character who can start a clue-label scene: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: Hand over the card with the printed pretend coat pocket visible, and keep all clues imaginary museum labels on paper: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a museum scene where the character notices one label that does not match its exhibit: ____________________.
cards.characterNamePrompt: Name the fictional clue-label tower character: ____________________.
cards.pocketItemPrompt: Write the pretend paper-pocket item, such as a blank tag, tiny stamp, or folded exhibit note: ____________________.
cards.wantPrompt: Write what the character wants the museum visitors in the story to understand: ____________________.
cards.worryPrompt: Write the character's worry about the mixed-up clue label: ____________________.
cards.actionPrompt: Write one action the character takes to compare two imaginary labels: ____________________.
cards.voicePrompt: Write one thoughtful line the character says while studying the clue: ____________________.
cards.reviseCharacterPrompt: Revise by adding one surprising thing the character is good at noticing: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the mixed-up label and the character's first guess: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home slip: Make a new fictional museum role and one pretend paper-pocket label: ____________________.

cards.title: The North-Needle Apprentice
cards.characterSkill: Builds a character through tools, decision-making, and a specific strength under pressure-free conditions.
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led paper card to support a fictional compass-craft character in a printable character-building activity: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: Put this card beside the printed pretend coat pocket and invite the writer to choose only imaginary craft materials: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a scene where the apprentice tests a compass craft and learns something about how they make choices: ____________________.
cards.pocketItemPrompt: Write the pretend paper-pocket item, like a paper needle, painted bead, or folded direction card: ____________________.
cards.wantPrompt: Write what the character wants their compass craft to point toward: ____________________.
cards.worryPrompt: Write one worry that could make the character rush, guess, or doubt themselves: ____________________.
cards.actionPrompt: Write the careful action the character takes before deciding which way to turn: ____________________.
cards.voicePrompt: Write one line that shows the character thinking through the choice: ____________________.
cards.reviseCharacterPrompt: Revise by adding one small flaw that makes the character more interesting but still kind: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write a three-part character note: tool, want, worry: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home slip: Finish this new compass character idea: My pretend paper-pocket tool points toward ____________________.

cards.title: The Button-Thread Boardwalk Binder
cards.characterSkill: Connects a character's promise, pocket object, and ending choice so the character feels complete.
cards.useCase: Use this adult-led paper card when a writer needs a fictional boardwalk character with a clear ending arc: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: Set the card on the table with the printed pretend coat pocket showing; all boardwalk details should stay fictional and paper-based: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write a scene where the boardwalk binder uses a pretend pocket item to help finish a loose story page: ____________________.
cards.characterNamePrompt: Name the fictional binding-day boardwalk character: ____________________.
cards.pocketItemPrompt: Write the pretend paper-pocket item, such as a button card, thread tag, or folded page corner: ____________________.
cards.wantPrompt: Write the promise the character wants to keep by the end of the scene: ____________________.
cards.worryPrompt: Write the worry that makes keeping the promise feel uncertain: ____________________.
cards.actionPrompt: Write the action that shows the character choosing how to bind the ending together: ____________________.
cards.voicePrompt: Write one line the character says when they understand what the ending needs: ____________________.
cards.reviseCharacterPrompt: Revise by adding one earlier clue that makes the ending choice feel earned: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write the promise and the final choice only: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home slip: Create another fictional binder and the pretend paper-pocket item that completes their story: ____________________.
